questiontext.text:
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int_0^{@upper_limit_x@} \int_0^{@upper_limit_y@} \int_0^{@upper_limit_x@} {@question_func@} dx dy dz = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places)

generalfeedback.text:
\( \text{Worked Solution}\)

\( \text{Recall that, just like with double integrals we start with the “inside” integral and work our way out.}\)

\( \displaystyle \int_0^{@upper_limit_z@} \int_0^{@upper_limit_y@} \int_0^{@upper_limit_x@} {@question_func@} dx dy dz \)

\( \text{Let's start by integrating wrt to x},\)

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \int_0^{@upper_limit_z@} \int_0^{@upper_limit_y@} {@x*coef_y*y*cos(z^(power_z))@} \displaystyle|_0^{@upper_limit_x@} dy dz & = \displaystyle \int_0^{@upper_limit_x@} \int_0^{@upper_limit_y@} {@coef_y*y*cos(z^(power_z))*upper_limit_x@} dy dz. \\ \displaystyle \int_0^{@upper_limit_z@} \int_0^{@upper_limit_y@} {@ta1@} dy dz & = \displaystyle \int_0^{@upper_limit_z@} {@coef_y*y^2*cos(z^(power_z))*upper_limit_x/2@} \displaystyle |_0^{@upper_limit_y@} dz\\ & \text{substituting y with {@upper_limit_y@} will give}\\ & =\displaystyle \int_0^{@upper_limit_z@} {@ta2@} dz\\ &=\left ( {@int(ta2,z)@} \right )\displaystyle |_0^{@upper_limit_z@}\\ & \text{substituting z with {@upper_limit_z@} will give} \\ &= {@ta@} \end{align} \)

truefeedback.text: You needed to have started the integration by first computing the integral wrt to \(x\) , then wrt \(y\) and finally wrt \(z\). Not the other way round.
